### LRX-02 — Separate mirror interception from return eligibility

**Affected:** `sharedRules[id=LR-G14].wording`; **`spell-mirror` / UN-19** → `operationalCandidate.limitations`; corresponding manuscript paragraphs. The shared correction also governs **`soul-mirror` / R3-09**.

The inherited wording first makes Touch/healing/willing-recipient interception depend on a legal return target, but later says an illegal return **spends the ward and leaves the original recipient**. Those branches disagree.

**Corrected rule:**

> A Touch-delivered, healing or willing-recipient spell is eligible for interception when it satisfies the existing sole-recipient and scope requirements. Spend that eligible ward before testing whether the original caster satisfies the payload’s actual return type, consent and other eligibility. An illegal or blocked return leaves the original recipient; the ward remains spent. A legal Touch return needs no new physical touch or Action.

This preserves the final source verdict’s stated spent-failure outcome. **Soul Mirror’s existing individual wording and LR-B05 already agree** and need no additional rewrite.

Acceptance cases must establish that an ineligible or nonconsenting return recipient does not preserve the ward or cancel the original spell for free. Excluded area/multitarget effects and countered spells still do not spend it. An already redirected root neither redirects again nor consumes the second mirror. Original caster ownership and the single effect packet remain unchanged.

### LRX-03 — Complete Bone Archer’s existing unarmed fallback

**Affected:** **`summon-bone-archer` / NE-23** → `operationalCandidate.resolution`, `.effect` and `.numericParameters`, in both envelopes and its manuscript.

The submitted effect permits an unarmed fallback, but the resolution describes commanded attacks only as ranged and supplies no complete unarmed modifier or reach.

**NEW completion of that already permitted option:**

> Instead of its bow attack, one permitted commanded offensive Action may make one unarmed melee attack at **+0 versus AC**, **reach 5 feet**, dealing **flat 1 bludgeoning** on a hit. Add no proficiency, ability modifier or extra damage die. Natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits but does not double the flat 1. Either attack spends the same shared commanded offensive allowance. This creates no extra attack, autonomous offense or additional Reaction permission.

The fixed modifier is an explicitly local exception to LR-G11’s owner-spell-attack default for this fallback only.

**KEEP** the bow’s original-caster spell attack modifier, **60/120-foot range and 2d6 piercing**, plus HP20, AC13, movement, command phase, concentration and no-resource ending.

The new numeric fields are:

```json
{
  "unarmedAttackModifier": 0,
  "unarmedReachFeet": 5,
  "unarmedFlatDamage": 1
}
```

Acceptance includes the natural-20 flat-damage result, reach rejection, missing-command rejection, and rejection after the bow has already spent the shared offensive allowance.

### LRX-05 — Resolve two inherited clock conflicts

**Affected:** **`false-footsteps` / IL-15**, **`echo-cast` / UN-21**, their specified operative fields, and the `LR-C-IL-15` example.

#### False Footsteps

“One pass each numbered round” conflicts with “manifestation plus the next two regular starts” when a legal readied release occurs before the caster’s regular slot.

**Keep the precise three-checkpoint procedure:**

> Resolve exactly three scheduled passes: the first at effect manifestation, then one at each of the next two future caster regular-turn starts. Expire at the third future regular-turn start measured from manifestation. These are instance checkpoints, not a separate once-per-numbered-round allowance. Extra turns add no checkpoint. For generic Ready, manifestation is release, not paid preparation. Suppression spends a scheduled pass without a later replay.

A readied release early in **round 5**, before the caster’s normal slot, therefore permits passes at **release in round 5, regular start in round 5, and regular start in round 6**, with expiry at regular start in round 7. There is no fourth pass.

Keep the range, path, at-most-six-second passes, acoustic restrictions and absence of compelled pursuit. Preparation still records the casting transaction once; it does not emit premature sound.

#### Echo Cast

“Next regular turn/next numbered round” is not one unambiguous window when a genuine extra-turn Action arms the spell before the caster’s regular slot.

**Keep the literal next-numbered-round promise:**

> Record the numbered round in which the Echo Cast arming spell is committed, including paid generic Ready preparation. Its replay is available only during the caster’s regular turn in the immediately following numbered round and expires at that turn’s end. A still-upcoming regular turn in the commitment round and every extra turn are ineligible. The arm must actually have manifested and remain unspent; a missed opportunity does not roll forward.

Preserve that scheduled window through the existing virtual-clock mapping. A held Ready retains its own concentration and earlier expiry; a manifested Echo arm does not newly require concentration.

An extra-turn arming in **round 4 before regular turn 4** cannot replay during regular turn 4; its window is regular turn 5. Paid Ready preparation in round 4 followed by a legal release before regular turn 5 retains that turn-5 window.

The replay still requires its real Action, same-class access, components and fresh resolution, with **only base RP waived**. **Quick Cast retains its different next-regular-turn rule.**
